additional_info.subject: ID0376669-DC/Si-D/DE[160355321] - EVSE Stop ohne Zutun des Fahrers CRM:00315001700
additional_info.body:
Hello colleagues﻿,﻿
Thank you for reaching out to eMobility Support. My name is
Francisco
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
MP / N8 160355321
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
cxGiFJ
Problem Description
: Charging session interruption due to DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101 error.
Troubleshooting
:
Through AWS I checked this last month and we only had 5 instances of this error.
What I request of you is, if you are able to get this error, immediately contact me as I want to check via EcoG frontend what is the temperature sensor reading
. If the temperature is indeed high then I believe there are some possibilities on why it's getting very hot:
Plug connected to the EV is somewhat twisted causing the contacts to overheat.
Too many charging sessions in a row
Plug's temperature sensor is getting faulty.
Unfortunately, I cannot recommend buying a new cable since it's only been 5 instances this last month.
For future reference, your ticket number is
0376669
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Francisco de Matos Joaquim

additional_info.subject: ID0376669-DC/Si-D/DE[160355321] - EVSE Stop ohne Zutun des Fahrers CRM:00315001701
additional_info.body:
Hi Rudi, good morning.
Francisco here, as you requested this ticket to go to the VI queue, I personally took it since we had to align together in the team. You might not know but I am part of the VI team but from the L2 so if you ever have any problem related to VI you can actually discuss with me.
From our perspective, this error has nothing to do with Vehicle Integration, it's a charger related issue and not the EV.
As such please continue with the investigation as I previously sent:
Make sure that the Plug's conditions are okay and also the EVs
Take a photo of the plug's contacts to see if they are not damaged.
Since it started occuring more and more:
Either the plug's temperature sensor is getting worse
There was an activity done on the charger after this specific date and as such there might be some loose connection/connector.
If you are able to get the error live, I can check remotely if it's correct and how the pattern looks like.
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0376669-DC/Si-D/DE[160355321] - EVSE Stop ohne Zutun des Fahrers CRM:00315001701
additional_info.body:
Hi Rudi, good morning.
I believe you don't need to send a technician just for this information:
Make sure that the Plug's conditions are okay and also the EVs
Take a photo of the plug's contacts to see if they are not damaged.
Since it started occuring more and more:
Either the plug's temperature sensor is getting worse
There was an activity done on the charger after this specific date and as such there might be some loose connection/connector
.
Confirm this one for me.
From AWS we can see that from the last 2 weeks, there was only 2 instances where this happened and it was in a short range of 30mins. The second session indeed ended with the error again, but since it's HPC, I really need to condition of the plugs to see if there is any problem.
Here is a photo of another region with the same problem:
This is the photo that I want, it might be that the contacts of the plugs are not good and are overheating or there is some dust/grain of sand, whatever it is, to make the contact between outlet and plug not good and this can cause overheat.
Please also check the EVs plug conditions.
Since the error rate is very low, I believe there is no problem with the sensor or the plug.
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco
